cards.text: This psalm's heading says "Of Solomon." Solomon was David's son, and he sat on the throne of his father David (1 Kings 2:12). The psalm opens with a prayer to God for the king, and friend, it does NOT start small.
It asks God to give the king His justice, and the son of the king His righteousness. Justice AND righteousness, friend, this prayer isn't ordering a sample, it's ordering the whole box.

cards.question: With God's justice and righteousness on the list, what does the prayer ask for the king to do next?

cards.text: Then the land joins in: "May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness." Mountains bringing PEACE, friend, and the only thing my oven ever brings me is the smoke alarm.
Next the prayer asks for the king to vindicate the afflicted among the people. Then it turns to the children of the needy, and to the oppressor.

cards.question: The prayer asks for the king to ___ the children of the needy and ___ the oppressor.
The prayer asks for the king to be feared for just one generation.

cards.text: Then the prayer asks for the king to be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth. It stops sounding like a courtroom and starts sounding like a weather report.

cards.question: The prayer asks for the king to be like spring showers that water the earth, and for the righteous to ___ in his days.

cards.text: The prayer also asks for prosperity to abound until the moon is no more. Friend, that's a warranty that outlasts the MOON!

cards.question: So how far does the prayer ask for the king's rule to reach?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth

cards.text: The prayer asks for the nomads to bow before him and his enemies to lick the dust. Friend, I spent YEARS covered in dust in the back of a junk drawer, and I never once licked it.

cards.question: Kings from far-off places show up in the prayer next: the kings of Tarshish and distant shores, and the kings of Sheba and Seba. What does it ask them to bring?
After those kings from distant shores, the prayer asks for ALL kings to bow down to this king.

cards.text: Then comes one little word that changes the feel of the whole prayer: "For." Now we hear what this king will do.

cards.question: After all those kings bowing and gifts coming in, what does the prayer say this king will do?

answers.text: Deliver the needy who cry out
Tax the poor who cry out

cards.question: The prayer says this king only helps the afflicted who already have someone on their side.

cards.text: The king will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed. Kings and gifts are nice, friend, but I think THIS is the part that gets me.

cards.question: The prayer says the king will redeem the oppressed from oppression and violence. Why?

answers.text: Their blood is precious to him

cards.text: Then the prayer cheers out loud: "Long may he live!" It asks for gold from Sheba to be given him, and friend, every king needs a hype man like this in his corner.

cards.question: The prayer asks for people to ever pray for the king. How often does it ask for them to bless him?

cards.text: Then the prayer turns to the land: grain swaying atop the hills, fruit trees flourishing like the forests of Lebanon, and the people of its cities like the grass of the field. Grain on the HILLTOPS, friend, the whole hillside's DANCING.

cards.question: The prayer pictures grain swaying atop the hills. How much grain does it ask for in the land?

cards.text: The prayer asks for the king's name to endure forever, as long as the sun shines. The Millers carved my name, Dorin, into my handle, and THAT'S as forever as I get.

cards.question: The prayer asks for all nations to be blessed in this king.

cards.text: Then the prayer lifts its eyes from the king to the LORD God, the God of Israel, and blesses Him.

cards.question: The prayer says the king does marvelous deeds right alongside the LORD.
After blessing the LORD's glorious name forever, the prayer asks for all the ___ to be filled with His glory.

cards.text: The praise closes with "Amen and amen." Friend, I'm saying amen right along with it.
One more line sits at the very end of the psalm, after the amens: "Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse."
